speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me the baby's age, how long they've been vomiting, and whether the vomit has been bilious? Also, have they had any bowel movements since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since the newborn is only six hours old with bilious vomiting, I need to know if any stool has passed yet, and if so, what was its color and consistency? Also, is the abdomen distended?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any stool yet, specifically meconium, and is the abdomen visibly distended? I will also request an abdominal X-ray to look for any signs of intestinal obstruction. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-ray shows a 'double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia. Physical examination reveals a distended upper abdomen and a concave-shaped lower abdomen with tympanic sound on percussion in the upper abdomen. No organomegaly or masses were palpable, and bowel sounds are normal. Vital signs are within normal limits.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal X-ray showing a "double bubble" sign, combined with the early bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance in this newborn, is classic for duodenal atresia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia
